chunks: (Or) one of those who created rifts in their order and are divided into sects, with each group exulting in what it has (carved out for itself) --
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about religious sects and their attitude towards their own beliefs?
ai.summary: In Surah Ar-Rum (30:32), this verse critiques the pre-Islamic and early Muslim tendency toward sectarian fragmentation, where each group ('shia') becomes complacent in its own dogma. Shia scholarship often contrasts this blind partisan joy with the unity of the Ahl al-Bayt, viewing the verse as a warning against rigid adherence to specific sects that lose sight of the core message of Islam.
